correctness.rationale: The claim is an exact finite extremal statement with an all-length consequence. An exhaustive normalized search generates every \( rac{7}{4}\)-free Dean word through length 68 by testing each newly created suffix for every possible forbidden period. It finds 414112 normalized words at length 67 with exactly one having \(d_3\ge3\), and 486776 at length 68 with none. Every length-68 word is pair-complete, so minimal absent triples can only disappear under extension. A separate full-factor scan verifies the displayed length-67 witness, its exact set \(D_3=\{010,101,303\}\), palindromicity, and the eight-element symmetry orbit.

value.rationale: Lemma 19 is a named finite obstruction in the source paper's trade-off between repetition threshold and the number of avoided length-three factors. Determining that its cutoff is attained and classifying every equality case is a natural complete boundary result. The unique-orbit statement is stronger than merely finding a single witness and gives a reusable exact benchmark for this Dean-word regime.
